description: SGLang fork serving natlang's LFM3 RL actors (owner decision 2026-10-29: upstream-maintained Liquid LFM3 implementation, sgl-project/sglang PR #46858, for dependability). The PR branch (with the upstream main it contains) plus natlang commits: exact post-temperature sampled-token logprob and top-k returned compactly per token (custom_params.natlang_top_k); LFM3 producer spans (the export's producing embedding table, span state mapped in extend and decode) and the native-state export of a closed span (custom_params.natlang_capture) and native-state import through content-hashed placeholders (custom_params.natlang_import), and per-request native adapters in resident low-rank slots (custom_params.natlang_adapter; batches without an adapted request replay the base-only decode graph). The natlang serving front is serve/sglang_actor.py (scripts/neuralese_data/serve_native_checkpoint.py --engine sglang); the checkpoint is served through export/native_hf.py. NATLANG_FORK.md in the fork documents the base, our commits and the rebase procedure. A separate git checkout, not vendored.
install: uv venv -p 3.12 VENV && uv pip install -p VENV/bin/python -e ../sglang-natlang/python --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
parity: scripts/neuralese_data/check_sglang_lfm3_parity.py (LFM3 logits: chunked prefill and cached decode against the vendored HF reference)
scripts/neuralese_data/check_sglang_producer_parity.py (producer spans and span export against native_step: perturbed adapter, forced and decoded spans, BF16 noise floor)
scripts/neuralese_data/check_sglang_adapter_parity.py (native adapter stacks through resident slots against run_native)
scripts/neuralese_data/check_sglang_hybrid_swa.py (hybrid SWA KV against the previous fork commit: greedy, prefix hits, Neuralese imports, retract/update_weights; `pair` runs both)

previous_commit.note: Prior fork head (tool grammars). Live actors import the DGX checkout (still 17e3458c2e) until it moves at a boundary with no live actor; held results pair within one fork commit. Its adapter slots are unsafe (the front serves no slots on it: serve_native_checkpoint.adapter_slots_on_fork).

qualification: The explicit FFN-only execution profile and SGLang dispatch have CPU coverage only. Native and SGLang whole-model state, actor/learner replay, held behavior and performance remain unqualified.
bf16_reduction: NATLANG_BF16_REDUCTION defaults to fp32-accumulate; reduced is historical replay only
projection: NATLANG_SGLANG_PROJECTION (serve_native_checkpoint.py --sglang-projection): native = the learner's invariant native_step projection kernel; vendor = one fused vendor BF16 GEMM per projection with fp32 accumulation, an actor law the learner recomputes and corrects with importance weights under the engine-mismatch guard (rl/native_replay.py).
top_k_mass: custom_params.natlang_top_k_mass: records end with the exact FP32 tail mass (review F6); the natlang front already sends and reads it. Merged into the fork branch natlang and pushed 2026-11-09. The declared commit is advisory: the actor attestation records the fork checkout's actual commit.
hybrid_swa_kv: ace8d6868 (2026-11-13): LFM3's 5 sliding layers keep only their 256-token window in SGLang's SWA pool, the 6 full layers every token (KV 11 -> 6 layers + 0.1 x 5 in the SWA pool; 16 GB FP8 holds 2.40M instead of 1.42M tokens). The front sizes the pool from the fork's NATLANG_HYBRID_SWA_KV marker (serve_native_checkpoint.py --sglang-swa-ratio 0.1; --sglang-full-kv opts out) and attests serving_engine.kv_layout. Engine identity changes with the fork commit: held results pair only within one fork commit, so the start policy is re-measured on it. NOT adopted by running experiments: enters at the next experiment boundary (ops/decisions.log 2026-11-13). Parity: scripts/neuralese_data/check_sglang_hybrid_swa.py (FP8 run against 70b1991e6: deterministic sections bitwise identical; the BF16-KV pair remains to run at a boundary gap).
track_input_end: 33230160b (2026-11-14, branch natlang, child of ace8d6868 = natlang head): custom_params.natlang_track_input_end makes the scheduler cut a request's prefill so its last extend is a whole number of 256-token grids, so the extra_buffer conv state lands exactly on the input end (PrefillAdder._natlang_input_end_extend); no forward, kernel or CUDA-graph change. The front reads the NATLANG_TRACK_INPUT_END marker (attest_sglang_source) and sets it on the request that warms a decision's shared opening (sglang_actor._sglang_warm_opening): every input then prefills only its own messages; on older forks the state stays up to 255 tokens short. CPU unit tests only (fork test/natlang/test_track_input_end.py); NOT adopted by running experiments, whose engine.json pins stay: it is the pin of the next experiment, which also adopts ace8d6868's hybrid SWA KV. Fast-forwarded into branch natlang 2026-11-14 (the branch natlang-track-input-end is gone); running experiments are unaffected because they pin commits.
import_host_cache: dd2430793 (2026-11-15, branch natlang, child of 33230160b): NatlangImport caches imported state files in host memory, bounded at 4 GiB, and moves only the gathered rows to the device. The device cache of up to 64 whole state files filled the ~0.8 GB Pop's 8 GB GPU keeps beside the KV pool and OOM-killed its held-eval engine every 45-90 min (grpo-v2-run2's base held-v3 measurement: 3 crashes, 63 of 512 episodes unscored, excluded from pairs). Indexing only: outputs unchanged. CPU tests: fork test/natlang/test_natlang_import.py. Like ace8d6868 and 33230160b it enters at the next experiment boundary: the DGX and Pop checkouts stay at 70b1991e6 while grpo-v2-run2 runs.
import_cache_bound: 1839b5071 (2026-11-15, branch natlang, child of dd2430793): NATLANG_IMPORT_CACHE_GB sets NatlangImport's host cache bound (default 4 GiB, unchanged); Pop's driver runs 0.5 (pop_actor_driver.serve_sglang: the actor unit has 10.5 GB of a 14 GB host). Configuration only, outputs unchanged. CPU tests: fork test/natlang/test_natlang_import.py. Enters at the next experiment boundary with dd2430793.
native_state_files: b6b2319c7 (2026-11-16, branch natlang, child of 1839b5071): native state crosses between the front and the fork as files of the natlang block store's own format. custom_params.natlang_capture carries the state's metadata (native_state) and the fork writes the span with natlang serve.store.write_native_state_file; the front adopts it into its store by rename, verified from the file (layout, finite values, content id), never decoding the tensors; natlang_import gets the stored block file itself (no import copy) and NatlangImport reads only its layers.* tensors. Front and fork move together: the front refuses a fork without the NATLANG_NATIVE_STATE_FILES marker (attest_sglang_source native_state_files). A new attested engine: the next experiment pin moves both checkouts and re-measures the start policy. CPU tests: fork test/natlang/test_natlang_capture.py, intake; natlang tests/neuralese/test_native_state_store.py, test_sglang_actor.py.
conv_bounded: dbc51ddb72 (2026-11-16, branch natlang, child of b6b2319c7; fast-forwarded into natlang 2026-11-16 for the grpo-v4 pin): natlang_conv_prefill reduces bounded 256-row blocks instead of materializing the whole prefill chunk's K-fold FP32 windows (Pop's held engine OOMed there on its 8 GB card). Same per-row expression, bitwise equal to the previous outputs on the DGX (sm121: fork test/registered/natlang/test_lfm3_native_conv.py, 39/39 fork natlang tests on dbc51ddb72); sm89 (Pop) bitwise test runs at the pin. Enters at the next experiment boundary with b6b2319c7.
fp8_weights: ec27f0809a (2026-11-22, branch natlang, child of dbc51ddb72): online FP8 weights (--quantization fp8 over the BF16 natlang export) run in LFM3's natlang projection paths (natlang_fp8_projection; they refused any quantized layer) and reload in place (load_weights stages BF16 shards, Fp8LinearMethod.natlang_requantize_online writes the existing FP8 weight/scale storage, so CUDA graphs keep valid buffers). Marker NATLANG_FP8_WEIGHTS: serve_native_checkpoint serves BF16 (sglang_weight_dtype_fallback) on a fork without it or a GPU below sm_89. BF16 serving is unchanged (the FP8 branches run only for natlang_online_fp8 layers). Checked on the DGX (sm_121) against the sft-v9 collection policy 66422fcf: fork test test/registered/natlang/test_lfm3_fp8_weights.py (requant bitwise = fresh quant, pointers unchanged); live server reload sft-v8->sft-v7->sft-v8 export gives bitwise the fresh prefill log-probabilities (512 tokens); FP8 vs BF16 prefill log-probabilities of 8,160 FP8-sampled tokens: mean |d| 0.053, median 0.001, p99 0.54, mean d +0.0017 (plans/neuralese/DECISIONS.md 2026-11-22 FP8 collection weights). Collection actors only; held and GRPO stay BF16. The DGX checkout moves to it at a boundary with no live actor.
tool_grammar: 17e3458c2e: the grammar backend loads the served tokenizer under --skip-tokenizer-init, and custom_params.natlang_grammar_prefix makes a continuation request's grammar take its trailing input ids first (NATLANG_GRAMMAR_PREFIX marker); the front (serve/sglang_actor.py) sends the common/tool_grammar.py structural tag and records it as the capture's sampling_law.tool_grammar. Tests test/natlang/test_grammar_prefix.py.
shared_graph_wrappers: 7a29eff9ee (2026-11-24, branch natlang, child of 17e3458c2e; doc 6c4a42b624): the decode graphs captured at one batch size (the adapter slots' 'lora' and 'nolora' variants) share that size's FlashInfer wrappers (and TRT-LLM MLA decode metadata). Before it the 'lora' graph replayed against wrappers the 'nolora' capture replaced and GC freed: CUDA illegal memory access in adapted decode (Colab L4 program-tune adapter arm; reproduced on the GB10 at 64 running, FP8 KV, chunk 4096) or attention over a stale plan. NATLANG_SHARE_GRAPH_WRAPPERS=0 opts out; marker NATLANG_SHARED_GRAPH_WRAPPERS, without which serve_native_checkpoint serves no adapter slots (adapted turns on the native engine). CPU tests: fork test/natlang/test_graph_variant_wrappers.py. Base-only batches are unchanged in arithmetic. Enters running experiments at their next pin (the DGX checkout moves at a boundary).
